background_notes.fact: A countable family of covering sets can be indexed by N, listing every original index once and padding unused indices by empty sets. For nonnegative costs with empty-set cost zero, this preserves the covered union and the extended sum. Conversely every N-indexed family is countable.

grounds.reason: H uses countable covers with nonnegative diameter-power costs and zero cost for empty members.
M002 uses N-indexed covers with zero empty-member cost.
The same positive exponent and finite positive scale are fixed on both sides.

background_notes.justification: An infinite countable index set admits a bijection with N; a finite index set can be placed in an initial segment with empty sets elsewhere. The covered union is preserved. An extended nonnegative sum is the supremum of finite subsums, so reindexing bijectively and adjoining zero terms preserve it. Thus both descriptions give the same attainable covering costs and infimum.

background_notes.fact: For each positive finite extended scale r, its real value delta>0 gives the same diameter-bounded covering infimum in M002 and D003 at exponent s>0. If C(r) is the M002 covering infimum, C(infinity)<=C(r) for every such r; consequently sup_{r>0} C(r)=sup_{delta>0} C(delta) even when these values are infinite.

background_notes.justification: At finite scale every admissible diameter is finite; embedding its real value into the extended nonnegative reals preserves the bound and its positive real power, including zero diameter. A supremum over proofs of nonemptiness is the constant cost if the member is nonempty and zero otherwise. BG001 handles indexing. Covers admissible at a finite scale are also admissible at infinity, so infimum monotonicity gives C(infinity)<=C(r), with no attainment needed. In particular C(infinity)<=C(1)<=sup_{delta>0}C(delta). All other positive scales are finite and correspond to positive reals, proving both inequalities for the outer suprema.
